subject: Mathematics
topic: Rational Numbers on the Number Line
title: Rational Numbers on the Number Line
summary: To place p/q, cut each unit into q equal parts and count p parts from 0: right for positive, left for negative.

notes.title: 02 – Rational Numbers on the Number Line

keyPoints: **Denominator q** = how many equal parts in each unit.
**Numerator p** = how many parts to count from 0.
Positive → count right; negative → count left.
Between any two rationals there is another: their average (a + b)/2.

blocks.alt: Number line from −2 to 2 with 3/4, 5/3 and −1/2 marked
blocks.caption: 3/4, 5/3 and −1/2 placed by cutting and counting.

list: Draw the line and mark 0, 1, 2, … (and −1, −2, … if needed).
Cut **each unit** into q equal parts (q = denominator).
From 0, count p parts: right if positive, left if negative.

blocks.p: Between 1/2 and 3/4 lies their average (1/2 + 3/4)/2 = **5/8**; between 1/2 and 5/8 lies 9/16; and so on forever. There are **infinitely many** rationals between any two.
**Common mistakes:** cutting the whole visible line instead of each unit; counting tick marks instead of the gaps; putting −1/2 to the right of 0.

quiz.q: To place 5/3, each unit is cut into:
quiz.explain: The denominator (3) tells how many equal parts per unit; then count 5 parts.

quiz.q: Between which two integers does 11/4 lie?

quiz.explain: Cut each unit into 2 parts and count 1 part to the left of 0.

quiz.q: A rational number between 1/3 and 1/2 is:
Do 1/2, 2/4 and 3/6 land on different points?
options: No, all on the same point
quiz.explain: Equivalent fractions are the same number, so they land on one point.

simulation.reason: Placing any p/q by cutting each unit and counting parts, including improper and negative fractions, is a procedure students learn best by doing; the existing fractions simulation only covers −1 to 1 without improper fractions, so a focused one was built.
simulation.objective: Place any fraction on the number line by cutting each unit into q parts and counting p of them.
instructions: Set p and q with the + and − buttons (or pick an example).
Press Cut and count: each unit is cut into q parts, then p parts are counted from 0.
Read where it lands and between which integers it lies.
Try a negative and an improper fraction.
